items.title: GeoAI for Sustainable Futures: Integrating Artificial Intelligence, Earth Observation and GIS for Environmental Resilience
items.abstract: Abstract Geospatial artificial intelligence (GeoAI), the integration of artificial intelligence with Earth Observation (EO) and Geographic Information Systems (GIS), is reshaping how environmental resilience is monitored and managed. This paper reviews GeoAI as both a technical practice and a geographical problem, arguing that its value for resilience planning depends on respecting the spatial properties — dependence, heterogeneity and scale — that distinguish geographic data from ordinary tabular data. The paper synthesises published evidence across four resilience-relevant domains: land use/land cover (LULC) change detection, drought risk assessment, landslide hazard zonation and groundwater potential mapping and situates this evidence within the Deccan Plateau and Western Ghats margin of Maharashtra, a terrain that compresses escarpment landslide risk, valley land-use change and rain-shadow drought within a single administrative region. The review finds consistent but bounded accuracy gains from machine-learning methods over conventional GIS overlay, with the largest gains reported where training and validation data are collected locally rather than transferred from elsewhere. The paper closes with a phased adoption roadmap for a teaching-and-research college operating in this terrain, arguing that institutional investment in ground-truth data collection should precede investment in more elaborate models.

items.title: Gobekli Tepe Was Not a Place but a Connection(괴베클리테페는 장소가 아니라 접속이었다)
items.abstract: This interdisciplinary and speculative essay reinterprets Göbekli Tepe, a Pre-Pottery Neolithic complex in southeastern Anatolia, not only as “humanity’s first temple” but as a periodic point of connection where ritual, exchange, feasting, dispute mediation, marriage, information, and collective memory may have converged. Beginning with a linguistic intuition inspired by the Proto-Indo-European root ters-, Latin terra, the Korean word teo(터), meaning a site or foundation, and the Turkish tepe, meaning hill—without claiming that these words share a common etymology—the essay asks whether a highly visible hill could have served as a recurring meeting ground connecting different ecological zones through multistage networks of people and goods. It develops a series of related hypotheses: marine shells, obsidian, hides, grain, pigments, and other materials may have reached Göbekli Tepe through relay exchange; animal reliefs may have identified participating groups; T-shaped pillars may have functioned as public memory devices recording contributions and promises; feasts may have settled obligations and renewed trust; sacred taboos may have provided security and judicial authority; and marriage may have maintained long-distance networks through kinship. The essay also places the Hwandan Gogi’s account of human differentiation, the biblical stories of Cain, the Flood, and the Tower of Babel, and Korea’s sodo sanctuary tradition alongside archaeological, genetic, and linguistic materials. These narratives are not presented as direct proof of Göbekli Tepe’s function, but as sources of questions concerning human gathering and dispersal, the formation of trust, the breakdown of exchange networks, and the emergence of centralized power. Ultimately, the essay proposes Göbekli Tepe as a prehistoric operating system and shared memory device: not merely a single temple or settlement, but an institution through which scattered human groups, goods, technologies, beliefs, and memories may have briefly synchronized. It also reflects on human–AI collaboration as another form of connection, distinguishing established evidence from inference and imaginative hypothesis while allowing each to generate new questions. 이 글은 선토기 신석기시대의 유적인 괴베클리테페를 단순히 ‘인류 최초의 신전’으로 보는 기존의 틀에서 벗어나, 제의와 교역, 잔치와 분쟁 중재, 혼인과 정보 교환, 공동체의 기억이 한곳에서 결합했던 정기적인 접속점으로 다시 상상하는 융합적·가설적 에세이다. 인도유럽조어의 어근 ters-, 라틴어 terra, 사람이 자리 잡고 관계를 형성하는 기반을 뜻하는 한국어 ‘터’, 언덕을 뜻하는 튀르키예어 tepe에서 출발한 언어적 직관을 통해, 이 글은 서로 다른 어원을 하나로 단정하는 대신 멀리서도 확인할 수 있는 언덕이 여러 생태권과 인간집단을 연결하는 반복적인 모임터였을 가능성을 묻는다. 지중해의 조개와 아나톨리아의 흑요석, 산악지대의 가죽과 레반트의 곡물 같은 물산은 여러 단계의 중계망을 통해 괴베클리테페에 도달했을 수 있다. 동물 부조는 참여 집단을 식별하는 표지였고, T자형 석주는 각 집단의 노동과 기여, 약속을 기억하는 공개 장부였을 수 있다. 잔치는 물자와 호의를 결산하고 신용을 갱신하는 절차였으며, 신성한 금기와 제의는 폭력을 억제하고 판결과 계약을 보증하는 치안·사법 장치였을 가능성이 있다. 혼인은 서로 떨어진 집단을 혈연으로 연결하며 교역망을 장기적으로 유지하는 수단이었을 것이다. 이 글은 또한 《환단고기》의 인류 분화 이야기, 성경의 카인과 대홍수·바벨탑 이야기, 한국의 소도 전통을 고고학·유전학·언어학 자료와 나란히 놓는다. 이러한 기록과 신화는 괴베클리테페의 기능을 직접 증명하는 사료가 아니라, 인류의 모임과 분산, 신용의 형성과 붕괴, 교역망의 단절, 중앙집권적 권력의 출현을 새롭게 질문하게 만드는 사유의 출발점으로 사용된다. 궁극적으로 이 에세이는 괴베클리테페를 선사시대 교역망의 운영체제이자 공동의 기억장치로 제안한다. 그곳은 하나의 신전이나 정착지에 머물지 않고, 서로 다른 인간과 물산, 기술과 신앙, 혼인과 정보가 잠시 동기화되었던 제도적 접속점이었을 수 있다. 아울러 이 글은 인간과 인공지능의 협업 역시 서로 다른 사고체계가 만나 새로운 질문을 만들어내는 또 하나의 접속이었음을 기록한다.

items.title: Green Intelligence 5.0: Designing a Net-Positive Digital Future through Artificial Intelligence, Environmental Sustainability, and Human Well-being
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming a general-purpose layer across education, healthcare, agriculture, energy, manufacturing and governance. It can strengthen climate-risk mapping, renewable-energy forecasting, precision irrigation, biodiversity monitoring, waste sorting and early-warning systems. Yet AI is not immaterial: computation depends on electricity, cooling, water, hardware, minerals, networks and labour, while rapid equipment turnover adds to electronic waste. This paper asks how AI can be designed so that its verified benefits for people and the planet outweigh its lifecycle burdens. Using an integrative evidence-synthesis and conceptual framework approach, the paper proposes Green Intelligence 5.0, a six-pillar architecture integrating ecological responsibility, responsible AI, circular infrastructure, inclusion, human well-being and accountable governance. Three practical contributions are introduced: the GROW-AI operating model, a 30-point Green Intelligence Scorecard, and a Net-Positive-by-Design decision rule. Recent global indicators illustrate the scale of the challenge: the International Energy Agency estimated data-centre electricity use at about 415 TWh in 2024 and projects approximately 945 TWh by 2030 in its base case; the Global E-waste Monitor reported 62 billion kg of e-waste in 2022, with 22.3% documented as formally collected and recycled. These figures are presented as sourced contextual indicators, not as original measurements by the authors. The framework is mapped to SDGs 3, 4, 7, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13 and 16, with an India-focused proposition: “AI for All, Green by Design.” The paper concludes that digital progress should be assessed by net human and planetary value—not computational scale alone.

items.title: Harnessing Digital Tools An Application for Productive Teaching, Writing, Research, and Reporting
items.abstract: This qualitative action research explored teachers' experiences in using artificial intelligence (AI) and digital tools for lesson preparation, academic writing, research, and reporting at Gapok Central Elementary School, Sultan Kudarat, Philippines. The study examined teachers' perceptions of the usefulness of these tools, their influence on instructional and administrative responsibilities, and the benefits and challenges associated with their integration. Sixteen teachers with experience using AI-powered applications participated in the study. Data were gathered through semi-structured interviews, focus group discussions, and classroom observations and were examined using thematic analysis. Six themes emerged: enhanced teaching efficiency and creativity, reduced workload and stress, research support and professional growth, accessibility and inclusive education, challenges in AI adoption, and support and readiness for integration. Participants reported that digital tools facilitated lesson preparation, supported the development of instructional materials, simplified research-related activities, and improved the organization and timeliness of reports. They also described greater confidence in using technology and opportunities to accommodate diverse learning needs. However, unreliable internet connectivity, limited familiarity with AI applications, device constraints, and the need to contextualize generated materials remained significant concerns. Despite these challenges, teachers expressed willingness to strengthen their digital competencies through training and peer collaboration. The findings suggest that AI and digital tools can support teacher productivity and professional development when accompanied by appropriate infrastructure, practical training, and responsible implementation. Strengthening institutional support and promoting collaborative learning may help schools integrate these technologies more effectively into everyday educational practice.

items.abstract: This scientific monograph introduces the Hierarchical Multi-Agent Verification and Dual-Axis 8-Layer Autonomous Governance Architecture (HQAS-8), designed and developed by HM Shihabuddin Jashory (Shihab). Grounded in first-principles algorithmic decomposition and empirical verification, HQAS-8 establishes a 4-tier adversarial chain-of-command (Worker, Supervisor, Chief Auditor, and Supreme Inspector General) coupled with deterministic pre-tool/post-tool execution gates and lifelong anti-regression experience memory (Hermes Ledger) to eliminate hallucination, context compaction drift, and unverified execution in production AI agent pipelines.

items.title: History of Indian Environment and the Role of Artificial Intelligence: An Analytical Study of Water Management, Climate Change, and Digital History Research
items.abstract: Abstract The development of Indian civilization is the story of the inter-relationship between water, land, forests, agriculture and human society. The town planning and drainage system of the Indus Valley Civilisation, ancient knowledge of water in India, ponds-wells-dams-canals, water planning by Malik Ambar, water resources and forts during the Maratha rule and the shifting control during the colonial period are subjects that can be explored under the umbrella of environmental history. Issues such as climate change, dwindling ground water resources, erratic rainfall, urbanisation and water contamination are becoming more complex today. Consequently, the linkage between historical knowledge and digital tool and AI becomes critical. The primary goal of this study is to look at the traditional system of water management in Indian environmental history, understand the potential of AI, GIS, satellite imagery, OCR and big data analysis in the field of digital history research and explore the correlation between historical environmental knowledge and sustainable development. Historical texts, inscriptions, maps, archaeological reports, digital archives, research articles, and current water resources information have been used in the study analytically.

items.title: How Do Older Workers in Germany Experience the Digitalisation of Their Workplaces?
items.abstract: Older workers in Germany are increasingly expected to work digitally, yet little is known about how they experience digitalisation. Drawing on waves 3 (2018) and 4 (2022/2023) of the representative German lidA cohort study on work, age, health and work participation, this chapter examines (a) the extent of digitalised work, (b) satisfaction with digital technologies at work, and (c) digital self-efficacy (DSE) among older workers. The analysis uses a longitudinal sample of employees born in 1959 and 1965 (Sample A, N = 2,112) and a cross-sectional sample including an additional 1971 cohort (Sample B, N = 7,406). Results show that almost all older workers use digital technologies at work, but overall digitalisation levels remained largely stable between 2018 and 2022/2023, with only a small shift from stationary to mobile computers. This result does not support the often-mentioned idea of a ‘digitalisation push’. Satisfaction with digital technologies is generally medium to high and did not change significantly over four years. About two thirds of workers report high DSE, yet a regression analysis indicates significantly lower odds of high DSE in older cohorts compared to the youngest cohort. Overall, these findings challenge deficit-oriented views of older workers but highlight a sizeable group with low DSE as a potential risk group for diminished workability and digital exclusion. Implications for occupational health and safety, HR practice, and German digital policy are discussed.

items.title: How should junior doctors navigate artificial intelligence clinical advice?
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) clinical decision support tools are becoming increasingly integrated into medical decision-making, offering rapid, evidence-based clinical recommendations. While surrounding discussion has largely focussed on senior clinicians, junior doctors, responsible for many day-to-day decisions in hospitals, face unique challenges in navigating these technologies among the many existing information sources. This paper examines the epistemic, ethical and practical implications of AI use by junior doctors, highlighting its potential to streamline knowledge access, as well as risks including automation, bias and deskilling. We introduce a suggested framework to help junior doctors navigate AI clinical advice and integrate it safely into clinical practice, among other information sources.

items.abstract: Generative AI (GenAI) is increasingly used by students to learn programming, yet it remains unclear how the intensity of its use relates to self-regulated learning (SRL). This study examined the relationship between GenAI usage intensity and SRL in programming among informatics engineering students. A cross-sectional correlational survey was conducted using convenience sampling (n = 86). Usage intensity was measured by frequency and duration of use over the previous 30 days and expressed as estimated hours per week. SRL was measured with a 16-item adapted version of the Self-Regulation of Learning Instrument for Undergraduates, grounded in Zimmerman's cyclical model. Data were analyzed using Spearman's correlation. Usage intensity showed a weak positive correlation with SRL (ρ = 0.272, p = 0.011). In exploratory analyses, duration of use, but not frequency, remained associated with SRL. The findings are correlational and should be interpreted cautiously.

items.title: HUMAN ROBOT COLLABORATION AND AI-ENABLED WAREHOUSE SAFETY MANAGEMENT FOR SUSTAINABLE LOGISTICS OPERATIONS IN SAUDI ARABIA
items.abstract: Robotic warehousing offers opportunities to reduce hazardous manual transport while introducing new risks at shared workstations, aisle intersections and digitally coordinated handovers. This critical integrative review evaluates how human-robot collaboration and artificial intelligence can support safer, more sustainable logistics operations, with Saudi Arabia as the proposed implementation context. Thirty DOI - indexed publications dated 2020 - 2025 were purposively examined across operational research, ergonomics, robotics, occupational safety and logistics management. Evidence was organised around exposure pathways, collaborative task allocation, predictive sensing, safety assurance, workforce acceptance and organisational governance. The synthesis shows that robotics may reduce walking and handling demands, but operational benefits cannot be equated with verified injury reduction. Adaptive speed control, transparent intention signalling, fatigue - aware scheduling and human - centred training appear promising when embedded within independently validated safeguards. Conversely, sensor uncertainty, deadline pressure, opaque algorithmic decisions and fragmented system ownership may transfer rather than remove risk.

items.title: Human Tutoring, Generative AI Tutoring, and Independent Internet Search: A Randomised Between-Subjects Experiment on Students’ Responses to Academic Challenge
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly available as a source of interactive academic support, raising questions about how it shapes learning. Research has focused on performance outcomes, with less attention to learners’ behavioural and affective responses to academic challenge, even though productive engagement with challenge supports deeper learning. In this randomised between-subjects experiment, students aged 16–18 at an English sixth-form college worked on two sections of challenging mathematics questions with one of three forms of support: one-to-one human tutoring, a GenAI tutor or unguided internet search. Measures included self-reported effort and perceived difficulty, questions attempted, post-task stress and subsequent challenge-seeking. Support condition was associated with different response patterns. Students using the GenAI tutor reported higher effort and perceived difficulty than those receiving human tutoring by the second section. Descriptively, post-task responses showed a lower proportion of stressed responses under GenAI tutoring than internet search. Human tutoring showed the lowest perceived difficulty and highest number of attempts in both sections, although significant pairwise differences varied by section. It also showed descriptively the lowest proportion of stressed responses. Challenge-seeking did not differ by condition and was instead strongly associated with trait challenge-seeking. The findings suggest that the GenAI tutor used in this study offered a form of support distinct from both human tutoring and unguided internet search, with potential value during independent practice rather than as a replacement for human teaching. They demonstrate the importance of evaluating AI-supported learning beyond performance outcomes and through behavioural and affective responses to difficulty.

items.title: Human Validation Layer: Constitutional Coherence Through Human-Governed Refinement
items.abstract: Large language models and automated decomposition systems can scaffold, decompose, index, and draft semantic structures at a scale that unaided review cannot match. Scale, however, does not establish fidelity, admissibility, authority, evidence, or global coherence. This paper proposes the Human Validation Layer (HVL) as a governed review and adjudication surface for deciding whether machine-generated or machine-assisted semantic artifacts may be promoted toward binding state. HVL is neither an assertion that humans are infallible nor a synonym for proofreading. It is a protocol in which accountable reviewers inspect typed artifacts, preserve source custody, record findings, surface disagreement, and either promote, hold, revise, split, merge, escalate, contest, or refuse. Condexing names the preparation of Pre-Crystallized Material (PCM) into non-binding Context Index (CONDEX) artifacts. A Condexer prepares reviewable evidence candidates; only an actor or procedure with the required authority may admit or bind them. The core claim is deliberately bounded: human participation can provide an accountable promotion boundary when its jurisdiction, evidence, criteria, conflicts, reasons, and authority are explicit and receipted. Human presence alone establishes none of those properties. The paper defines validation objects, role separation, promotion policy, failure modes, evaluation requirements, and interfaces with the Governed Meaning Base (GMB), Governed Context and Memory, semantic custody, governed semantic compilation, lexical and structural binding, authority-laundering tests, and reasoning by way of receipts.

items.title: Human Values in the Digital Era
items.abstract: Abstract The digital era has transformed communication, education, work, commerce, governance and social interaction. Artificial intelligence, social media, smartphones, digital platforms, cloud services and data-driven systems have created unprecedented opportunities for access to knowledge and participation. At the same time, digital life has intensified ethical questions concerning privacy, truth, dignity, empathy, responsibility, justice, equality, autonomy and human well-being. This conceptual research paper examines the significance of human values in the digital era and explores how technological progress can be guided by a human-centred ethical framework. The paper is based on a qualitative conceptual review of selected books and educational and policy-oriented literature related to human values, technology, digital citizenship, ethics and education. The analysis indicates that technology itself is neither automatically beneficial nor harmful; its social consequences depend substantially on the values embedded in its design, use and governance. The paper identifies respect, responsibility, honesty, empathy, compassion, justice, privacy, digital self-discipline, critical thinking and sustainability as important values for responsible digital life. It further argues that educational institutions have a central role in developing value-based digital citizenship by integrating ethical reasoning, media literacy, information literacy, cyber safety and reflective use of technology. A balanced approach is required in which innovation is encouraged while human dignity and social responsibility remain at the centre. The paper concludes that the future of digital society should be evaluated not only by speed, efficiency and intelligence, but also by whether technology strengthens human relationships, democratic participation, inclusion and holistic well-being.

items.title: Human-in-the-Loop Governance for Agentic AI: Security, Accountability and Decision Control in Enterprise Business Analysis
items.abstract: Agentic AI systems plan and act through tools (code execution, database queries, file access, network requests) that enterprises now use for business analysis, and the governance of these systems depends on where a human is kept in the loop. This study asks where human approval gates should sit, how rapidly the software layer through which agents act is being secured, and how accountable its disclosure practice is. The study used every GitHub-reviewed security advisory affecting 365 LLM-application and agent packages on PyPI and npm (N = 2,172 advisories across 346 packages, through 4 October 2026) and mapped each exploit path, using its CWE class, to the control point at which a gate could intercept it. The design is event-historical and Bayesian rather than regression-based: Kaplan–Meier and package-stratified Cox models of vulnerability dwell time and post-disclosure remediation, Bayesian hierarchical models with package random effects for autonomous exploitability, severity and fix-at-disclosure, and a Bayesian decision analysis of gate configurations. Advisory volume rose sharply in 2026 (81.9% of records), led by MCP tool servers and agent frameworks. Agent-action surfaces (prompt injection, execution, queries, file access, network requests and data egress) account for 52.6% of advisories and are more severe but not more autonomously exploitable than platform flaws; the median dwell time of vulnerable code is 248 days and 79.2% of advisories are fixed at disclosure, but the package, rather than the surface, governs remediation speed and most late fixes never arrive. Five approval gates would intercept 59.6% (95% credible interval 55.3–64.0%) of the 499 high- or critical-severity paths that need neither user interaction nor privileges, with execution and egress gates contributing most and returns diminishing quickly. Residual risk, computed as 1 − e × coverage for an assumed, rather than observed, reviewer effectiveness of e, stays above 0.46 at e = 0.9 and cannot fall below 0.40 even with a perfect reviewer, so gates complement rather than replace platform controls. The findings ground a three-tier Human-in-the-Loop Governance Framework (security gates, accountability ledger, decision-control authority) for agentic business analysis.

items.title: Human-Resource Digital Transformation Trends in Private Universities in India
items.abstract: The digital transformation is reshaping the functioning of academic, administrative and human-resource operations in higher education institutions. The study focuses on the implementation of digital HR in the private Universities of India, specifically on the following digital HR practices: payroll automation, employee self-service, online recruitment, digital performance appraisal, learning management systems, artificial intelligence (AI), and HR analytics. The descriptive survey design was adopted and the data were obtained from 60 HR professionals and administrative personnel in private higher education institutions. The results indicate that high adoption of payroll automation and employee self-service portals and on the other hand, AI-based recruitment and HR analytics are still in their early stages. Financial challenges, employee resistance, lack of digital skills, integration of systems and data-security issues are the main challenges identified. The results have shown that the HR automation process in private Universities is moving from simple automation to more sophisticated and data-oriented HR processes; however, sophisticated digital HR is still at its beginning stage.

items.title: Human–Artificial Intelligence Collaboration in Intelligent Information Systems for Supporting Organizational Decision-Making
items.abstract: The use of artificial intelligence in information systems is increasingly influencing organizational decision-making processes, but its effectiveness still depends on how humans understand, assess, and use AI-generated recommendations. This study aims to explore the pattern of human–AI collaboration in intelligent information systems and its contribution to organizational decision-making. The research uses a qualitative approach with a case study design. Data were collected through in-depth interviews with 15 managers, analysts, and users of AI-based information systems, then analyzed using thematic analysis. The results show that decision effectiveness is influenced by the human–AI role sharing, trust in the system, recommendation transparency, and user interpretation ability. The findings confirm the importance of system design that places AI as a support for human considerations in decision-making.

items.title: HUMAN–GENAI INTERACTION MODES IN PROGRAMMING EDUCATION
items.abstract: Generative AI (GenAI) tools are becoming part of everyday learning in higher education, especially in programming courses where students can ask for explanations, debugging help, or complete code. This creates an important educational question: not only whether students use AI, but how they interact with it. This study compares three Human–GenAI interaction modes in an introductory object-oriented programming course: No AI, AI Tutor, and Direct AI. Thirty students completed three C# programming tasks under a within-subject classroom design with a balanced rotation of task order. The study examined completion time, code quality, measured understanding, perceived difficulty, and students’ subjective evaluations. The Direct AI task–mode combination was associated with the strongest product-oriented outcomes: shorter completion time (Mdn = 10 min), higher code scores (M = 9.20/10), and the highest completion rate (96.7%). AI Tutor and No AI showed longer completion times and lower code scores. However, measured understanding varied little across modes (M = 3.57–3.70/4), with all medians at the maximum score, indicating a ceiling effect. The raw-score product–understanding gap was largest under Direct AI (M = 5.50), reflecting a stronger increase in code scores than in measured understanding. Student perceptions added a different perspective: 70.0% selected AI Tutor as the most effective mode for learning, while 90.0% selected Direct AI as the fastest. The findings suggest that unrestricted AI support can optimise task completion and product quality, but these gains should not be read as equivalent to learning gains. Guided AI Tutor interaction may be educationally valuable because it is designed to preserve more of the student’s reasoning process. Because each mode was paired with a specific task, the results should be interpreted as task–mode combination differences rather than isolated causal effects of interaction mode. The study contributes empirical evidence for designing GenAI-supported programming activities and assessment practices that distinguish product-oriented performance from learning-oriented outcomes.

items.title: Implementation and Evaluation of a Blockchain and Decentralized Identity-Based Federated Learning Prototype for GPT-2 Fine-Tuning
items.abstract: Large language model development depends on large-scale training data, yet centralized collection raises privacy risks and concentrates control among a few organizations. Federated learning addresses part of this problem but retains a central aggregator, cannot readily verify contributions, and lacks sustained incentives. Blockchain integration resolves coordination and transparency, yet participant identity remains exposed to sybil attacks. This study designs, implements, and evaluates a prototype platform combining these three technologies. The prototype uses GPT-2 Small with 10,000 Alpaca samples partitioned Non-IID across five clients, the FederatedHub contract on Ethereum, and IPFS as off-chain storage. Evaluation covers 5 rounds across 3 seeds, 9 attack variants, a sybil attack using 10 identities, and two-attacker collusion. The delta-based scoring function yields scores from 27.3 to 73.0 correlating 0.920 to 0.991 with data volume, perplexity falls from 24.6722 to 7.7798, and ROUGE-L rises by 106.6%. The gate catches 8 of 9 variants, yet one variant that positions itself inside the acceptance range passes every trial while capturing 95.2% of legitimate client rewards. All sybil identities are admitted, and gas cost limits the system to 15 or 16 participants. The weakness lies in the identity and incentive layers, not in model quality.

items.abstract: This article examines how integrating artificial intelligence (AI) technologies, such as adaptive learning platforms, interactive simulations, and generative language models, into physics teaching can improve the quality of knowledge among academic lyceum students. A pedagogical experiment comparing AI-supported instruction with traditional methods showed higher conceptual understanding, analytical thinking, and motivation in the experimental group, while also highlighting risks such as over-reliance on AI and the need for teacher guidance. The findings indicate that, when used systematically and under teacher supervision, AI technologies enhance knowledge quality and support student-centered physics education. items.title: INSTRUCTIONAL LEADERSHIP, EDUCATOR COMMITMENT AND MOTIVATION: EFFECTS ON HOLISTIC DEVELOPMENT IN KEMAS PRESCHOOLS, MALAYSIA
items.abstract: Holistic student development has become a fundamental indicator of educational quality in early childhood education because it encompasses children's cognitive, socio-emotional, physical, moral, and spiritual development. Despite increasing attention being given to holistic education in Malaysia, empirical evidence explaining how instructional leadership, educator commitment, and educator motivation contribute to holistic student development within KEMAS preschools remains limited. This study therefore examined the levels, relationships, and predictive influence of instructional leadership, educator commitment, and educator motivation on holistic student development among KEMAS preschool educators in the Northern Zone of Malaysia. A quantitative cross-sectional survey design was employed involving 313 educators selected from a population of approximately 1,700 educators across Kedah, Perak, and Pulau Pinang. Data were collected using structured questionnaires adapted from established instruments and analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson's Product-Moment Correlation, and Stepwise Multiple Linear Regression using SPSS. The findings indicated that instructional leadership, educator commitment, educator motivation, and holistic student development were all perceived at high levels. Significant positive relationships were identified between all independent variables and holistic student development. Stepwise regression analysis further revealed that extrinsic motivation emerged as the strongest predictor, followed by intrinsic motivation, providing incentives to students, and defining school mission and goals. Collectively, these predictors explained 42.1% of the variance in holistic student development. The findings provide empirical evidence supporting leadership enhancement, educator motivation, and evidence-based policymaking to strengthen preschool educational quality within KEMAS.

items.title: INTEGRASI ENERGI TERBARUKAN PADA SMART MICROGRID: OPTIMASI, FLEKSIBILITAS, RESILIENSI, DAN KECERDASAN BUATAN
items.abstract: ABSTRACT High renewable energy penetration is transforming smart microgrids from local generation systems into cyber-physical energy platforms that must coordinate planning, storage, flexible demand, electric vehicles, multi-energy coupling, market interactions, resilience, and intelligent control. This review synthesizes 56 Scopus-indexed records published in 2024-2026, all supplied in the reference extraction file, using a structured integrative review and thematic evidence synthesis. The literature was organized into six research fronts: joint sizing and energy-management co-design; flexibility portfolios based on batteries, hydrogen, pumped hydro, shared storage, and electric vehicles; transactive and multi-microgrid coordination; uncertainty-aware control and artificial intelligence; resilience and cybersecurity; and multi-energy sector coupling. The evidence shows a clear shift from isolated techno-economic sizing toward multi-objective, multi-time-scale, degradation-aware, and increasingly adaptive control. Recent studies also demonstrate that energy-management strategy can reshape the optimal physical design of a microgrid, while shared storage, peer-to-peer exchange, vehicle-to-grid, and hydrogen expand system flexibility beyond conventional batteries. However, the literature remains fragmented across planning and real-time control, physical and cyber resilience, technical optimization and market fairness, as well as simulation and field validation. The most defensible research gap is therefore not the absence of optimization algorithms, but insufficient end-to-end integration among co-design, uncertainty management, user behavior, lifecycle impacts, cybersecurity, and deployment constraints. A next-generation smart-microgrid framework is proposed to connect physical assets, sensing, forecasting, intelligent energy management, flexibility markets, multi-criteria objectives, and implementation feedback. Three linked priorities emerge: end-to-end multi-horizon co-design with degradation-aware flexibility, safe and explainable AI validated through HIL, field, and multi-site testing, and integrated physical-cyber resilience; market fairness and lifecycle governance are treated as cross-cutting constraints. ABSTRAK Penetrasi energi terbarukan yang semakin tinggi mengubah smart microgrid dari sistem pembangkitan lokal menjadi platform energi siber-fisik yang harus mengoordinasikan perencanaan, penyimpanan, beban fleksibel, kendaraan listrik, kopling multi-energi, interaksi pasar, resiliensi, dan kendali cerdas. Artikel ini mensintesis 56 rekaman terindeks Scopus periode 2024-2026 yang seluruhnya berasal dari file ekstraksi referensi yang disediakan, menggunakan tinjauan integratif terstruktur dan sintesis bukti tematik. Literatur dikelompokkan ke dalam enam frontier: co-design antara sizing dan energy management; portofolio fleksibilitas berbasis baterai, hidrogen, pumped hydro, shared storage, dan kendaraan listrik; koordinasi transaktif dan multi-microgrid; kendali sadar ketidakpastian dan kecerdasan buatan; resiliensi dan keamanan siber; serta kopling multi-energi. Bukti menunjukkan pergeseran dari sizing tekno-ekonomi yang terpisah menuju optimasi multi-objektif, multi-skala waktu, sadar degradasi, dan semakin adaptif. Studi terbaru juga menunjukkan bahwa strategi energy management dapat mengubah desain fisik optimal microgrid, sementara shared storage, peer-to-peer exchange, vehicle-to-grid, dan hidrogen memperluas fleksibilitas melampaui baterai konvensional. Meskipun demikian, literatur masih terfragmentasi antara perencanaan dan kendali real-time, resiliensi fisik dan siber, optimasi teknis dan fairness pasar, serta simulasi dan validasi lapangan. Gap utama bukan kekurangan algoritma optimasi, melainkan belum kuatnya integrasi end-to-end antara co-design, pengelolaan ketidakpastian, perilaku pengguna, dampak siklus hidup, cybersecurity, dan kendala implementasi. Review ini mengusulkan kerangka smart microgrid generasi berikutnya dan memprioritaskan tiga agenda yang saling terkait: co-design multi-horizon dengan valuasi fleksibilitas sadar degradasi, safe dan explainable AI yang divalidasi melalui HIL, lapangan, dan multi-lokasi, serta integrasi physical-cyber resilience; fairness pasar dan tata kelola siklus hidup diperlakukan sebagai constraint lintas tema.

items.title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence and Innovation Modules into Traditional Master of Business Administration Core Curricula to Enhance Modern Business Education and Leadership Readiness
items.abstract: Abstract: The paradigm of modern commerce has shifted irreversibly, driven by the exponential proliferation of artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, and disruptive technological innovations. Traditional Master of Business Administration (MBA) programs, historically anchored in static case methodologies and compartmentalized functional silos (e.g., finance, marketing, operations, and strategic management), face mounting pressure to bridge the gap between legacy pedagogy and contemporary industry demands. This paper examines the imperative for seamlessly embedding AI and innovation modules into core MBA curricula. By analyzing the systemic transition of AI from an experimental peripheral tool to an enterprise-wide operational architecture, this study outlines a comprehensive framework for cultivating digitally fluent, ethically grounded, and change-ready business leaders. We propose a holistic curriculum redesign that transcends isolated technical electives, infusing data literacy, algorithmic decision-making, prompt engineering, and human-centric innovation management directly into core business courses. Furthermore, the paper addresses institutional barriers, faculty readiness, and the delicate equilibrium between technical proficiency and foundational emotional intelligence. Ultimately, this research posits that modernizing graduate business education through structured AI and innovation integration is essential for safeguarding the societal relevance, practical efficacy, and leadership readiness of future executives.

items.title: INTEGRATION OF DIGITAL TECHNOLOGIES INTO THE PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT OF EDUCATORS: THE SLOVAKIAN EXPERIENCE
items.abstract: Slovak Republic has accumulated significant experience in integrating digital technologies into the professional development of educators, and a systematic analysis of this experience could serve as a resource for modernising the Ukrainian system of postgraduate education. The aim of this article is to provide a theoretical analysis, systematisation and classification of digital technologies for professional development of educators in Slovakia and to justify a model for professional development of educators using digital technologies. General scientific methods such as analysis, classification and systematisation of the results of scientific publications, as well as content analysis of strategic and regulatory documents of the EU and the SR, were employed. The article highlights the results of national and international projects implemented at Comenius University in Bratislava, which are aimed at supporting the professional development of teachers in digital environment. Strategic and regulatory documents, project materials, methodological resources and practices developed within the framework of national and international initiatives have been analysed, with particular attention paid to the DiTEdu project and the digital professional development of educators. Based on the systematisation and comparative analysis of the identified practices, an original structural-functional model of professional development for educators using digital technologies has been developed, and a classification of the main types of digital tools used in the Slovak context has been proposed. The findings have made it possible to identify the key organisational, pedagogical and technological conditions for effective digital professional development, in particular personalised learning, blended formats, professional networking, learning using artificial intelligence, the development of digital competence and ongoing methodological support. Recommendations are proposed at the national, institutional and individual levels for Ukrainian postgraduate education regarding the implementation of the Slovak experience in the using of digital technologies in the professional development of educators.

items.title: Inteligência artificial aplicada à saúde: avanços, aplicações, desafios éticos e perspectivas para a medicina contemporânea
items.abstract: A inteligência artificial (IA) tem apresentado crescente aplicação na área da saúde, contribuindo para o diagnóstico, apoio à decisão clínica, análise de dados, documentação e assistência aos profissionais. O objetivo foi analisar as principais aplicações da IA na saúde, destacando seus avanços, benefícios, limitações e desafios relacionados à sua utilização na prática clínica. Foi realizada uma revisão da literatura na base de dados PubMed, utilizando os termos de busca ("artificial intelligence "OR" machine learning" OR "deep learning" OR "generative artificial intelligence") AND ("healthcare" OR "health" OR "medicine"). Foram considerados estudos publicados entre 2020 e 2026, nos idiomas inglês e português, relacionados à aplicação da IA na saúde e na medicina. A busca identificou 19 trabalhos, dos quais 10 foram incluídos na revisão após a aplicação dos critérios de elegibilidade e 9 foram excluídos por não atenderem aos critérios estabelecidos. Os estudos incluídos demonstraram aplicações da IA em diagnóstico, análise de prontuários eletrônicos, identificação de eventos adversos, documentação clínica, saúde mental, consultas médicas e apoio à tomada de decisão. Os modelos de linguagem apresentaram potencial para auxiliar profissionais e otimizar atividades na área da saúde, embora tenham sido identificadas limitações relacionadas à geração de informações incorretas, vieses, qualidade das respostas, segurança e necessidade de validação clínica. Conclui-se que a IA apresenta potencial para contribuir para a transformação dos serviços de saúde, porém sua utilização deve estar associada à validação científica, supervisão profissional, proteção dos dados dos pacientes e estratégias para redução de erros e vieses. A tecnologia deve ser utilizada como ferramenta complementar à atuação dos profissionais de saúde.

items.title: Internal Audit and Artificial Intelligence: A Narrative Review of Governance Conditions for Audit Effectiveness
items.abstract: Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping organizational governance and, within it, the internal audit function. Research on AI in auditing has focused largely on external audit, on specific technologies or on ethical principles, and few contributions connect the theoretical foundations of governance and internal audit with the governance challenges that AI introduces. This paper therefore asks how AI is transforming internal audit and which governance conditions are required for this transformation to strengthen, rather than undermine, audit effectiveness, understood as analytical coverage, detection capacity, independence and quality of reporting. Based on a narrative and integrative review of 66 sources published between 1932 and 2026, and drawing on agency, contingency, neo-institutional, stakeholder and sociomaterial perspectives, the paper distinguishes data analytics, automation and AI in the strict sense, weighs the benefits of AI against its costs and limits, and develops a conceptual framework linking AI capabilities, AI governance mechanisms, the auditor's role and audit effectiveness, from which five theoretical propositions are derived. The review suggests that AI may enhance audit efficiency, broaden analytical coverage and strengthen fraud and anomaly detection, while simultaneously introducing governance risks related to algorithmic opacity, data quality, automation bias, accountability and auditor independence. The paper contributes by treating AI both as an audit tool and as an audit object, and by differentiating the managerial and regulatory implications for internal audit leaders, audit committees, senior management and regulators. It outlines precise research questions, hypotheses and designs for future empirical work, particularly in resource-constrained and public-sector contexts such as Moroccan public establishments. Résumé : L'intelligence artificielle (IA) transforme la gouvernance organisationnelle et, avec elle, la fonction d'audit interne. La recherche sur l'IA en audit s'est surtout concentrée sur l'audit externe, sur des technologies prises isolément ou sur des principes éthiques, et peu de travaux relient les fondements théoriques de la gouvernance et de l'audit interne aux défis de gouvernance que l'IA introduit. Cet article interroge donc la manière dont l'IA transforme l'audit interne et les conditions de gouvernance requises pour que cette transformation renforce, plutôt que fragilise, l'efficacité de l'audit, entendue comme la couverture analytique, la capacité de détection, l'indépendance et la qualité des rapports. Fondé sur une revue narrative et intégrative de 66 sources publiées entre 1932 et 2026, et mobilisant les perspectives de l'agence, de la contingence, néo-institutionnelle, des parties prenantes et de la sociomatérialité, l'article distingue l'analyse de données, l'automatisation et l'IA au sens strict, met en balance les bénéfices de l'IA et ses coûts et limites, et construit un cadre conceptuel reliant les capacités de l'IA, les mécanismes de gouvernance de l'IA, le rôle de l'auditeur et l'efficacité de l'audit, dont sont dérivées cinq propositions théoriques. La revue suggère que l'IA pourrait améliorer l'efficacité de l'audit, élargir la couverture analytique et renforcer la détection des fraudes et des anomalies, tout en introduisant des risques de gouvernance liés à l'opacité algorithmique, à la qualité des données, au biais d'automatisation, à la responsabilité et à l'indépendance de l'auditeur. L'article contribue en traitant l'IA à la fois comme outil et comme objet d'audit, et en différenciant les implications pour les responsables de l'audit interne, les comités d'audit, la direction générale et les régulateurs. Il formule des questions et des dispositifs de recherche précis pour de futurs travaux empiriques, en particulier dans les contextes contraints en ressources et dans le secteur public, tels que les établissements publics marocains.

items.title: Internet of Things (IoT): Applications, Benefits, Challenges and Future Scope
items.abstract: Abstract The Internet of Things (IoT) is a rapidly developing technology that enables physical objects to connect to the internet and exchange data with other devices and systems. These objects may include household appliances, vehicles, industrial machines, medical equipment, agricultural systems, and smart-city infrastructure. IoT combines sensors, communication networks, cloud computing, data analytics, and artificial intelligence to collect and process information and support intelligent decision-making. This research paper examines the concept and architecture of IoT, its major technologies, applications, advantages, challenges, security concerns, and future scope. The paper concludes that IoT has significant potential to improve efficiency, automation, safety, and quality of life across various sectors, although privacy, cyber security interoperability, and scalability remain important challenges.

items.title: Interpretability-driven feature engineering enables compact and accurate multi-outcome risk stratification at hospitalization for chronic hepatitis B
items.abstract: Clinical artificial intelligence (AI) often trades predictive performance against interpretability. This study develops an interpretability-driven feature engineering framework for multi-outcome risk stratification at hospitalization for chronic hepatitis B. A total of 36,024 hospitalization records from 22,001 patients were included. The framework integrating SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-based main and interaction effects was used to construct compact machine learning models for classifying disease non-progression, liver cirrhosis (LC), and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). SHAP main effects selected the top 15 features per outcome; TreeSHAP interactions selected four pairwise terms. Performance was evaluated using patient-level data splitting, temporal validation, and independent external validation, with calibration and decision-curve analyses. The full-feature models achieved superior discrimination (AUCs: 0.927, 0.897, and 0.899) for classifying hospitalization-recorded disease non-progression, LC, and HCC, respectively. The corresponding compact models maintained strong discrimination (AUCs: 0.911, 0.882, and 0.890) with 80.8% fewer features. Interaction models yielded subtle AUC shifts (AUCs: 0.912, 0.881, and 0.891) while characterizing potential clinical joint-effect patterns. Temporal validation yielded AUCs of 0.863, 0.827, and 0.847, while external validation yielded AUCs of 0.829, 0.865, and 0.827, respectively. The framework produced compact and transparent models for contemporaneous risk stratification in clinical practice, seamlessly uniting predictive accuracy with multi-level interpretability.

items.title: Intrinsic motivation improves performance with less effort than extrinsic motivation
items.abstract: Students may learn their course material for different types of motives: because the material is interesting or because they aim at a good grade. A common intuition is that performing tasks because they are interesting (under intrinsic motivation) requires less effort than performing tasks because they are instrumental for obtaining some benefits (under extrinsic motivation). Yet, this notion is not incorporated in current effort allocation models, which were developed in the context of instrumental behaviour. These same-cost models would consider intrinsic and extrinsic motivation as targeting two types of rewards through the same kind of effortful process. Here, we introduce a different-cost model, in which intrinsic motivation improves task performance by providing effortless direct drive, whereas extrinsic motivation improves performance through the exertion of effortful cognitive control. We tested the predictions of this model across a series of behavioural experiments, during which volunteers (n = 147 in total) memorized lists of information, with various levels of self-reported interest and various amounts of monetary reward associated to correct recall. Behavioural results indicate that both interest and reward (intrinsic and extrinsic motivation) improve memory performance, with no interaction between the two effects. Computational analyses show that these behavioural effects are best captured by the different-cost model, rather than the same-cost model. Moreover, pupillometry validated the key prediction of the different-cost model: for a similar improvement in performance, increasing interest triggers lesser effort exertion compared to increasing reward. Together, these findings suggest that working under intrinsic motivation might relax the demand on cognitive effort and help preventing fatigue and burnout syndromes. A new ‘different-cost’ model of effort allocation to learning under intrinsic vs. extrinsic motivation is tested across six studies combining behavioral tasks, pupillometry and computational modelling. Evidence is found in favor of the new model, showing that intrinsic motivation alleviates the effort cost attached to improving memory performance

items.title: Inverted MAML & Forward Hadamard Propagation (FHP): Physical Silicon Verification, Spatially Correlated LLM Benchmarks, and Multi-Layer Atomic Triads (SE 2630397-4)
items.abstract: Abstract This dataset and open-source hardware release presents the complete design, FPGA firmware, and physical silicon validation of Inverted MAML (Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning) Analog In-Memory Computing (AIMC) (Patent Application SE 2630397-4). The system implements an analog atomic triad matrix processor utilizing discrete Dual-2T1C differential analog triode multiplier cells for ultra-low-power, real-time matrix-vector multiplication with continuous closed-loop drift and temporal capacitor decay compensation. Key Innovations & Architecture Atomic Triad Analog Matrix Structure: Integrates primary payload compute (Matrix 33, 6×6), first-layer carrier modulation (Matrix 3, 8×6 with analog Sigmoid activation), and second-layer Vernier drift compensation (Matrix 8, 7×6) summing directly at the transimpedance amplifier (ColTIA) virtual ground. Forward Hadamard Gradient Extraction (Non-Backpropagation): Forward perturbation voltages (V_PTU) are orthogonally coupled via zero-DC Walsh-Hadamard sequences into 2T1C storage nodes while input vectors x are held stationary. Gradients are extracted in real time via Fast Walsh-Hadamard Transform (FWHT) directly from analog physics without digital backpropagation. Dual FPGA SoC Digital Control: Controlled by an Efinix Trion T120 BGA324 Master SoC (RISC-V Sapphire soft core, 100 Hz capacitor refresh engine, UDP telemetry streaming) coupled to an Efinix Trion T20 BGA256 Gate & Hadamard driver node. - **Milestone 1 & 2 Silicon Validation (Fixed 5.0 ms Operating Point):** - **Milestone 1 (In-Situ Gradient Extraction):** Validated on physical silicon that all partial derivatives can be extracted from an unknown analog neural network in single-shot O(1) time using Forward Hadamard Propagation (FHP) without backpropagation or mathematical transistor modeling. - **Milestone 2 (Dynamic Error Compensation):** Demonstrated on physical 2T1C silicon that active Inverted MAML elevates sustained resolution from a hardware ground floor of ~3.4 bits (43,003 LSB² loss) to ~4.0 bits ENOB (-59.6% quadratic loss) under continuous multivariate white noise across the entire input volume. - **Enhanced Performance on Correlated Vectors:** Spatially correlated autoregressive input vectors (LLM Toeplitz KMS AR(1), ρ = 0.85) yield even stronger compensation, elevating sustained precision to 5.79 bits mean ENOB with peaks reaching 7.13 bits. *(Milestone 3 active work-in-progress: Sweeping temporal discharge windows from 4.5 ms to 5.5+ ms to establish hardware decay bounds).* Package & Repository Contents Hardware CAD & EDA (v2.0): Complete EasyEDA Pro project files (.epro2), interactive schematics, Gerber fabrication files, Pick-and-Place (CPL), and verified Bill of Materials (BOM). FPGA Synthesis & Firmware: Verilog RTL synthesis projects for Efinix Trion T120 & T20, timing constraint files (.sdc), and RISC-V embedded C firmware with multi-strata batch update algorithms. Calibration & Telemetry Suite: Python real-time GUI, hardware UDP client, automated regression testers, and 500-epoch silicon telemetry datasets. Documentation & Engineering Reports: Detailed mathematical derivations of forward Hadamard gradient extraction, ColTIA saturation guard protocols, and PDF characterization reports. items.title: Investigating the Impact of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Transformation on Organizational Decision-Making, Human Resource Management, and Employee Productivity in the Electrical Power Industry
items.abstract: Background: Electrical power organizations are adopting artificial intelligence (AI), digital twins, advanced analytics, and workflow automation while facing aging infrastructure, changing load patterns, scarce specialist labor, and strict reliability obligations. Objective: This article investigates how AI-enabled digital transformation relates to organizational decision-making, human resource management (HRM), and employee productivity in electricity generation, transmission, distribution, and utility support functions. Methods: An integrative, structured narrative review of identifiable 2024-2026 peer-reviewed studies and reports from recognized research and standards organizations was undertaken. A cross-domain evidence matrix aligned operational use cases with organizational mechanisms, workforce outcomes, and assurance requirements. No primary interviews, experiments, or utility microdata were collected; thus no causal effect estimates are claimed. Results: The evidence supports a contingent model in which improved data availability and predictive capability can accelerate routine decisions, prioritize asset work, and support forecasting, whereas gains in human productivity depend on role redesign, training, trust, interoperability, and oversight. Benefits differ materially between office-based knowledge work and physically performed grid tasks. Algorithmic HRM creates opportunities for workforce planning and skill development but can also magnify bias, surveillance, opacity, and stress. Conclusion: Digital transformation is better understood as a jointly technical and organizational capability than as software deployment. A staged, human-accountable governance architecture and a multidimensional evaluation scorecard are proposed for future empirical testing.

items.title: Investigation of musculoskeletal disorders, hand grip strength, wrist proprioception, reaction time and postural awareness in office workers at high ergonomic risk
items.abstract: Objectives. This study examined musculoskeletal disorders, handgrip strength, wrist proprioception, reaction time (RT) and postural awareness in office workers at high ergonomic risk. Methods. The cross-sectional study involved 150 office workers aged 25–45 years. Ergonomic risk was evaluated using the rapid office strain assessment, dividing participants into high-risk (n = 52) and low-risk (n = 98) groups. Musculoskeletal discomfort was assessed with the Cornell musculoskeletal discomfort questionnaire, pain intensity with the visual analog scale, handgrip strength with a dynamometer, wrist proprioception with a goniometer, RT with the choice ruler drop test and postural awareness with the postural habits and awareness scale. Results. Office workers with high ergonomic risk demonstrated significantly lower dominant and non-dominant hand grip strength and greater wrist joint position sense error compared with those without ergonomic risk (p < 0.05). Non-dominant extremity RT was significantly slower in the high-risk group (p = 0.013). Postural habits and awareness scores were significantly lower among workers at ergonomic risk (p < 0.001). Upper back musculoskeletal complaints were significantly associated with high ergonomic risk (p = 0.011). Conclusions. High ergonomic risk is associated with reduced neuromuscular performance and increased musculoskeletal symptoms among office workers. These findings emphasize the importance of ergonomic assessment and preventive interventions in office environments.

items.title: IoT-Based Lifting Posture Detection using Random Forest for WMSD Prevention
items.abstract: Work-Related Musculoskeletal Disorders (WMSDs) from improper lifting techniques remain a major occupational health concern globally. This study develops an Internet of Things (IoT)-based lifting posture detection system using Random Forest classification to enable real-time monitoring and early WMSD prevention. The system integrates two MPU6050 inertial sensors placed on the thoracic and lumbar regions, a BMP280 pressure sensor attached to the load (15-liter water gallon), an ESP8266 microcontroller, and a Flask-based web application with buzzer feedback. Data were initially collected from 24 participants, with 20 included in the final analysis after excluding incomplete datasets, generating 53 engineered features from acceleration, gyroscope, pressure, and orientation signals. The Random Forest model was evaluated using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation and achieved an overall accuracy of 83.32%, with the correct posture class showing higher recall (0.87) and F1-score (0.85) compared to the incorrect class (recall 0.79, F1-score 0.81). Feature importance analysis identified thoracic and lumbar pitch angles as key predictors of safe lifting biomechanics. Real-time system testing across 40 activities yielded a 97.5% prediction accuracy with an average confidence of 86.7%, demonstrating the system's practical viability. While the model shows promise for automated posture monitoring, performance variability across subjects (68.62%–96.20%) indicates the need for larger, more diverse training datasets and further algorithm refinement. This research establishes a foundation for IoT-based ergonomic intervention systems that provide immediate auditory feedback to reduce WMSD risk in occupational settings.

items.title: Istisarelism: Proportionate Objection, Epistemic Autonomy and Reasoned Termination in Human–AI Deliberation
items.abstract: This conceptual paper proposes Istisarelism as a provisional normative and methodological framework for reasoned, proportionate disagreement in human–AI deliberation. Seven principles govern the framework: fallibility, priority of reasons, within-dialogue revisability, proportionate objection, risk-sensitive caution, effective human autonomy, and reasoned termination. The proposal is compared with established human–AI deliberation, Socratic AI, critical-thinking interventions, appropriate reliance, and the 2026 AACT and SYNC frameworks. Its candidate operational mechanism, the Reasoned Objection Threshold (ROT), evaluates evidence, decision relevance, marginal informational contribution, conversational history, and cognitive cost, with separate safeguards for consequential risks. The paper distinguishes useful cognitive effort from redundant interaction burden. A two-arm feasibility pilot followed by a factorial study is proposed to isolate objection selection and termination. A prospective non-inferiority criterion for reasoning quality and a reduction in redundant objections jointly define the principal research aim. Research status: This is a conceptual preprint. No empirical results, independent peer review, or definitive priority claim are asserted. The paper presents a falsifiable research agenda rather than a validated new theory. Generative AI assisted with drafting and internal critical review. Responsibility for the research claims and publication rests with the human author.

items.title: Justifying the design of ai interventions in education: An analysis of teachers’ attitudes and a multi-layered readiness model
items.abstract: Introduction. The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into general secondary education is accompanied by a persistent gap between teachers’ declared readiness to use AI tools and their actual integration into the learning process. Teachers employ AI primarily for routine tasks, while its potential for transforming instruction and personalization remains unrealized, creating risks of cognitive debt for students and the erosion of professional agency. The lack of empirically grounded models for designing AI interventions that account for teachers’ attitudes and cognitive risks impedes pedagogically sound AI integration. This study aims to empirically substantiate a two-axis ‘cognitive offloading – agency’ model and a four-layer ‘AI Readiness – 4L’ model based on an empirical analysis of teachers’ attitudes, practices, and barriers to AI use, as well as to formulate architectural principles for AI interventions. Materials and Methods. The theoretical framework comprised a synthesis of the ‘Systems AI Readiness’ concept, the SAMR, SCOT, JTBD, and TPACK models, and Bandura’s social cognitive theory. The empirical basis was a mixed-method design (2024–2025) conducted across four comprehensive secondary schools in Tomsk (Russia). The quantitative component involved a survey of teachers (n=118); the qualitative component included interviews with school principals (n=3). Thematic analysis and case study methods were employed. Results. A ‘readiness paradox’ was identified: despite positive attitudes toward AI, less than a third of teachers regularly use AI tools, and the majority rate their AI competencies as insufficient. Differentiation in principals’ managerial positions was established. A two-axis ‘cognitive offloading – agency’ model with four types of interaction in the «student – AI – teacher» system was empirically substantiated. The critical risk of cognitive debt occurs when high offloading is combined with low agency. A four-layer ‘AI Readiness – 4L’ model (technological, social, needs-based, and competency layers) was developed. Social-organizational factors, rather than infrastructure, were found to be the key predictors of readiness. Architectural principles for AI interventions were formulated. The critical risk of cognitive debt occurs when high offloading is combined with low agency. A four-layer ‘AI Readiness – 4L’ model (technological, social, needs-based, and competency layers) was developed. Social-organizational factors, rather than infrastructure, were found to be the key predictors of readiness. Architectural principles for AI interventions were formulated. Conclusions. The proposed models and principles provide a foundation for designing AI interventions that leverage the transformative potential of technology while preserving teacher agency and student cognitive autonomy, confirming the necessity of transitioning to pedagogically mediated AI adoption.

items.title: KECERDASAN BUATAN GENERATIF DALAM PEMBELAJARAN BAHASA ARAB: SYSTEMATIC LITERATURE REVIEW TENTANG TREN, MANFAAT, TANTANGAN, DAN ARAH PENELITIAN
items.abstract: The landscape of foreign language education, particularly Arabic language instruction, is currently undergoing a fundamental transformation driven by the emergence of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) and Large Language Models (LLMs). This Systematic Literature Review evaluates recent developments in the integration of GenAI into the Arabic language learning ecosystem, encompassing trends in the evolution of language models, pedagogical effectiveness, the utilization of automated assessment systems, as well as the linguistic and cultural challenges involved. Through a thematic synthesis of empirical and theoretical literature published between 2019 and 2026, this review confirms that GenAI significantly enhances learner engagement, instructional personalization, and language skill acquisition, particularly in vocabulary mastery and reading comprehension. These improvements are driven by the adoption of general-purpose models such as ChatGPT, as well as leading Arabic-centric models such as JAIS and ALLaM. Nevertheless, this innovative integration encounters the inherent structural complexity of the Arabic language. Generative models frequently experience technical limitations in handling syntactic rules (nahwu), morphology (shorof), diacritic disambiguation, and regional dialect variations, as evidenced by performance gaps in linguistic benchmarks such as AraLingBench and AlGhafa. Furthermore, this review discusses rapid advances in trait-based Automated Essay Scoring (AES) supported by precise prompt engineering. Based on these findings, the study concludes that although GenAI has significant potential to bring positive disruption, its successful implementation depends heavily on pedagogical readiness, digital literacy, the application of Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) collaboration, and the development of ethical frameworks aligned with the epistemology of Islamic higher education.

items.title: La imagen proyectual: promptografías y agencia visual en el diseño
items.abstract: AI-generated images produced by generative artificial intelligence (GAI) appear to be altering the conditions under which ideas emerge in the design process. However, research on their cognitive effects during ideation remains fragmented and, at times, contradictory. This article does not present original empirical research; rather, its contribution is based on a critical and interpretive review of recent academic literature (2023-2025) on generative images, visual agency, and ideation in design and architecture. These images are examined as external supports of design thinking, in continuity with the graphic representations studied by Schön (1983) and Cross (2006), and read through the lens of distributed and extended cognition (Hutchins, 1995; Clark and Chalmers, 1998). The corpus was selected according to its relevance to three key issues: the cognitive function of GAI-generated images as supports for formal exploration, lateral thinking, and metacognition; the role of unexpected variations and “creative errors” as catalysts, or as sources of visual fixation, in design thinking; and the redistribution of creative agency imposed by these systems, shifting the act of design from execution toward selection, curation, and the critical reading of algorithmic output. The concept of the projective image is proposed to designate those generative images that do not translate a prior idea but instead constitute the site where the idea emerges. The review shows that GAI simultaneously produces thematic expansion and stylistic convergence, and that its effect on creativity depends more on the level of critical judgment exercised by the designer over the output than on the degree of intervention. The article argues that the productive integration of GAI into the design process requires an active critical stance toward the agency of the generated image.

items.title: Lifelong Memory Architectures for Large Language Model Based Generative AI Systems: A Survey and Comparative Analysis
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) form the basis of multiple generative applications today, but these systems are mostly stateless which means that information keeps outside the context window disappears when the session is closed. Such limitations complicate personalization, make it difficult to maintain consistency over long interactions, and prevent the AI system from learning from its experience. Lifelong memory architectures address this problem by providing the LLM with an external, permanent memory that also includes means of information writing, retrieval, updating, consolidating, and forgetting without the need to retrain the model itself. This paper presents an overview of the developments in this area starting from early external-memory enhancement and reflective generative agents, and continuing with memory operating system, graph-shaped memory, and reinforcement learning of agent memory. We summarize our results, suggesting an operation-centered classification of such systems and compare such twelve representations with regard to scalability, retrieval efficiency, personalization, computational cost, and adaptability, discussing necessary technologies such as embeddings, approximate nearest neighbor index, knowledge graph, and retrieval-augmented generation.

items.title: Literature in the Age of Emerging Technologies: New Perspectives and Possibilities
items.abstract: Abstract The relationship between literature and technology has always been dynamic. From the invention of the printing press to the emergence of digital books, social media, artificial intelligence, virtual reality, and other digital platforms, technological developments have continuously influenced the ways in which literature is produced, distributed, read, and interpreted. In the contemporary period, emerging technologies have created new possibilities for literary expression while also raising important questions about authorship, creativity, originality, reading practices, and the future of the literary text. Artificial Intelligence (AI), digital humanities, electronic literature, virtual reality, augmented reality, and online publishing are particularly significant in this transformation. This paper examines the changing relationship between literature and emerging technologies. The paper contends that we should not view technology solely as a tool for reproducing traditional literature. Rather, it has become an active force that changes the form, structure, circulation, and interpretation of literary works. Digital platforms have made literature more accessible and interactive, while artificial intelligence has introduced new possibilities for writing, translation, editing, and literary analysis. At the same time, these developments have generated concerns regarding plagiarism, copyright, authorship, misinformation, algorithmic bias, and the possible loss of human creativity. The paper therefore considers both the opportunities and challenges created by emerging technologies in literary studies. It concludes that literature is unlikely to disappear in the technological age; instead, it is evolving into new forms that require readers and scholars to rethink the meaning of authorship, text, reading, and creativity.

items.title: Mapping moral reasoning research among college students: a bibliometric analysis of traditional foundations and emerging digital ethics
items.abstract: The increasing complexity of ethical dilemmas in higher education, particularly those involving digital technology, has increased scholarly interest in college students’ moral reasoning. However, previous reviews have focused mainly on theoretical perspectives or ethics education interventions, with limited attention to the intellectual structure of this research field. This study maps the intellectual and thematic organization of research on college students’ moral reasoning and examines the emergence of digital ethics and artificial intelligence within the literature. A total of 677 documents published between 1983 and 2024 in the Web of Science Core Collection were analyzed using VOSviewer for co-citation and keyword analyses, following a PRISMA-based screening procedure. The findings show that Kohlberg’s theory of moral development and Rest’s Four-Component Model form major foundations of the field, while recent thematic developments include digital ethics, academic integrity, artificial intelligence, virtual simulations, and cross-cultural moral education. The study provides a systematic bibliometric knowledge map and identifies emerging and underexplored areas for future theoretical and empirical research.

items.title: Marketing Management in the Digital Era: An Integrated Framework for Customer Value, Data-Driven Decision-Making and Sustainable Business Growth
items.abstract: Abstract Marketing management is no longer about selling and promoting goods, but it is about creating, communicating, delivering and sustaining the value to the customers. Marketing managers have access to a range of new tools which have grown significantly due to digital platforms, social media, e-commerce, data analytics, marketing automation and AI. Meanwhile, there is ever more demand for relevance, convenience, transparency, personalisation, responsible data use and meaningful brand experiences. This is a conceptual research paper that addresses the nature of marketing management in the digital age and creates an integration of market orientation, segmentation and positioning, customer experience, digital communication, data-driven decision making, artificial intelligence, brand management, relationship marketing and sustainability. The psaper has been drawn from literature review of the existing marketing-management literature, digital-marketing literature and selected Marathi reference sources. The study is based on conceptual synthesis and managerial implications because there is no primary survey or fabricated numerical data. The review shows that the effective marketing management in the contemporary world needs a balance between technology and judgment of human beings. While Data and AI can enhance targeting, prediction, personalization and measurement, customer trust, ethical communication, privacy, brand purpose and human centred service are still vital. The paper suggests a practical sequence of actions: getting to know the market, customer value definition, identification of priority segments, the creation of an integrated value proposition, the activation of digital and physical touch points, measuring results, constant learning and embedding of responsible marketing. The framework is especially relevant for organizations that are in competitive, digital and rapidly changing markets.

items.abstract: The development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) provides opportunities to support the learning process, but it also presents challenges related to ethics, data security, academic integrity, and responsible use of digital technology. This community service activity aimed to improve AI literacy among students and parents by strengthening their understanding of safe, ethical, and responsible AI use. The activity was conducted at SDN 25 Madello over a two-month period, involving students and parents as participants. The method employed an educational-participatory approach through material delivery, discussions, practical activities, case studies, and evaluation. The materials covered an introduction to AI, the use of AI in learning, AI ethics, academic integrity, personal data protection and security, and legal awareness in the digital environment. The activity was conducted through collaboration among the fields of Education, Constitutional Law, and Islamic Family Law. The results indicated an improvement in participants’ understanding of the benefits and risks of AI use, as well as the importance of verifying information, protecting personal data, and using AI responsibly. The activity also demonstrated the importance of parental involvement in supporting children’s AI use at home. Cross-disciplinary collaboration provided a comprehensive approach to developing a generation that is aware, critical, and responsible in utilizing AI.
